4. The Underdog Upset Ticket: The Dogs and Why

How it works: 6 underdogs to win outright, combined into every two-team parlay — 15 combos × $1.33, $19.95 total. Payout by number of winners: returns (avg): 2 hit $12, 3 hit $35, 4 hit $70, 5 hit $116, 6 hit $175. Two winners does not turn a profit on this build; it needs three or more. Each dog is on the ticket because we think its chance of winning is better than its price implies — not because we expect all of them to win.

🐶 Jacksonville Jaguars +129 — JAX@CIN · tier 2 · our projection JAX 25 – CIN 27

Why it's on the ticket: Experts split 6–4. JAX: Action Network, Brandon Kravitz (The Favorites), Doug Kezirian, and three teasers through +8.5 (Steve Fezzik and Ross Tucker of Even Money, and Dave Tuley's VSiN best bet). CIN: Sharp or Square ("prime bounce-back spot for Burrow"), Jason Radowitz of BettingPros, Steve Makinen of VSiN (a best bet) and Mike Florio (Bengals 28–27). The money is the story: the JAX moneyline has 38% of tickets but 58% of the money, a 20-point sharp gap, and JAX has 63% of spread tickets and 62% of the money. One counterweight from Evan Abrams' primer: teams covering by 10-plus points a game over their first three (the Jaguars this week) are 47–72–3 against the spread in their next game over 15 seasons. The line has held at CIN −2.5 since the Action Network open; the total went up from 50.5 to 52. The lean is JAX +2.5, or the +129 moneyline, and JAX +8.5 as a Wong teaser leg through 3 and 7. The over is the consensus (Andrew Erickson at 51, BettingPros at 50.5), but it has moved 1.5 points and the projection sits on the number, so play Parker Washington's receiving instead of the total. Card: the JAX moneyline is in the Slot 2 Dog-ML 2-team RR and the 2-leg ARI ML + JAX ML ticket, and JAX +8.5 is a leg of the 6-pt Wong teaser JAX-DEN-ATL.

What breaks it: Jacksonville's +4 turnover margin regresses and Burrow gets a clean pocket all day; Chase hits two explosives and Cincinnati wins by a touchdown. If the moneyline money keeps coming and the line flips to JAX, the price is gone.

Card evidence: Big-money flag (38% tickets / 58% money); 6–4 named experts JAX; projection CIN by 2 · full game write-up

🐶 Denver Broncos +126 — DEN@SF · tier 2 · our projection DEN 23 – SF 24

Why it's on the ticket: This is the most one-sided expert game on the slate. DEN: Action Network, Sharp or Square, Steve Fezzik, BettingPros, Chad Millman (his "trade of the week," calling the reverse line move sharp), John Jastremski, Evan Abrams, Matt Moore, Andrew Erickson (+3) and Dave Tuley of VSiN (+8.5 in teasers, a best bet). SF: Mike Florio (49ers 24–20) and Steve Makinen of VSiN (−3, a best bet). Splits: SF has 60% of spread tickets and 64% of the money and 84% of moneyline tickets, yet the line came down from the Action Network open of SF −3 to −2.5. Every DEN +3 position is now +2.5, past the key number. The lean is DEN +2.5 or the +126 moneyline, plus McCaffrey receiving. On the total, 60% of the money is on the under against 52% of tickets, and the total is up from 45.5 to 48; small under lean. Card: the heaviest exposure on the card (about $85). The DEN moneyline is in the Slot 2 Dog-ML 2-team RR, the Slot 4 Afternoon parlay and the Slot 5 Hybrid; DEN +2.5 is a proposed SuperContest pick (both SuperContest tickets); DEN +8.5 is a leg of the 6-pt Wong teaser JAX-DEN-ATL. A 49ers win by 3 or more hurts six tickets at once.

What breaks it: The 49ers' offense, at 63% on third down, doesn't need Bosa to win a shootout: Kittle and McCaffrey beat the blitz and San Francisco wins by ten. Denver scores only 20 a game and can't keep pace if Nix is pressured. Mike Evans is a game-time decision with a rib injury (ESPN); recheck at the 11:55 PT inactive window.

Card evidence: 11–2 named experts DEN; SF −3 → −2.5 against 60%+ SF money; Bosa and M. Williams out; projection SF by 1 · full game write-up

🐶 Atlanta Falcons +112 — ATL@NO · tier 2 · our projection ATL 23 – NO 25

Why it's on the ticket: NO: BettingPros (twice; a Monday-night home spot), Pablo Planovsky of Action Network and Mike Florio (Saints 23–17). ATL: Sharp or Square (+3, a bottom-five Saints defense), Joe Gibbs (divisional home favorites are 12-18-1 straight up under this referee crew) Brandon Anderson (Falcons +2.5 in his four-team parlay), Steve Makinen of VSiN (+2.5; New Orleans is 4–14–1 against the spread in its last 19 Monday-night games), and Falcons +8.5 as a teaser leg from Dave Tuley (a best bet) and Wes Reynolds. Evan Abrams' primer adds the great-condition divisional road dog system on Atlanta, and the Saints have ruled out linebacker Kaden Elliss and pass rusher Carl Granderson. Splits: NO has 49% of tickets and 51% of the money on the spread, but the ATL moneyline is a big-money flag, 26% of tickets and 45% of the money. The line is unchanged at NO −2.5 since the Action Network open; the total is up from 47.5 to 48. The lean is ATL +2.5, or the +112 moneyline. BettingPros (46.5) and Pablo Planovsky (47.5) have the over; the projection sits on 48, so pass the total. Bookmaker props for this game weren't captured; this block gets a Monday rewrite after the 15:45 PT inactives. Card: the ATL moneyline is in the Slot 2 Dog-ML 2-team RR and ATL +8.5 is a leg of the 6-pt Wong teaser JAX-DEN-ATL; both settle Monday night. The Monday-night island ladder is built after the Sunday board.

What breaks it: Atlanta's turnover problem continues: two Penix giveaways and New Orleans wins by ten. If Fant plays, Olave gets single coverage more often and the Saints' HIGH matchup becomes a big passing day.

Card evidence: Big-money flag (26% / 45% money); Makinen, Gibbs, Sharp or Square, Anderson ATL; Saints out Elliss + Granderson; projection NO by 2 · full game write-up

🐶 Las Vegas Raiders +184 — KC@LV · tier 2 · our projection KC 25 – LV 22

Why it's on the ticket: LV: Sharp or Square (twice, "divisional home underdog"), Even Money (both hosts, best bet: Steve Fezzik and Ross Tucker), Pat Fitzmaurice, Simon Hunter, who already bet it, and Dave Tuley of VSiN (a best bet). KC: BettingPros (twice), Andrew Erickson, Derek Brown and Mike Florio (Chiefs 23–16). Splits: KC has 52% of tickets and 55% of the money on the spread, and the LV moneyline has 11% of tickets and 10% of the money, no gap. Evan Abrams' primer backs the Raiders: its home-dog-against-an-undefeated-team system is 101–66–4, and when two undefeated teams meet in Week 4 or later, the home team is 25–17–1 against the spread. The line moved toward the Raiders, from the Action Network open of KC −5.5 to −4.5. The lean is LV +4.5, with Bowers receiving as the prop. Total opinions lean under: Pat Fitzmaurice, Derek Brown and Steve Makinen of VSiN at 47.5 and Wes Reynolds at 48, against Fezzik (47.5) and BettingPros (46.5) on the over. With the projection at 47, that's a small under lean, not a bet. Card: the LV moneyline is in the Slot 2 Dog-ML 2-team RR (LV +4.5 is a SuperContest alternate), and Patrick Mahomes 2+ passing TDs is in the 7b Afternoon prop stack: a Chiefs win by 3 or less cashes both.

What breaks it: Mahomes and Walker score early, Cousins has to chase, and the +5 turnover luck reverses: a Kansas City win by ten. If Walker gets the red-zone work BettingPros expects, the Chiefs cover by scoring touchdowns instead of field goals.

Card evidence: Fezzik/Tucker + Tuley best bets LV +4.5; home dog vs undefeated system (101–66–4); projection KC by 3 · full game write-up

🐶 New York Jets +167 — NYJ@CHI · tier 1+2 · our projection NYJ 20 – CHI 23

Why it's on the ticket: The named experts favor New York on price: Steve Fezzik and Ross Tucker (Even Money, both at +3.5), Action Network's contest pick, BettingPros at +3, Wes Reynolds of VSiN (+3.5) and Kendra Middleton ("an even better spot if Bagent starts"). The CHI side is Mike Florio (Bears 27–17), Andrew Erickson's BettingPros primer (−3.5) and a BettingPros pick at −3.5 that was written around Case Keenum starting. Dave Tuley of VSiN passes. ESPN and Pro Football Talk both report that Bagent is expected to start, the condition Kendra Middleton named. Splits lean Chicago, 57% of tickets and 62% of money, no sharp gap; the NYJ moneyline has 13% of tickets and 18% of money. The line went from the Action Network open of CHI −3 to −3.5. The lean is NYJ +3.5 for the hook; the projection lands on the 43 total, and the only total signal is a wind-under system in Evan Abrams' primer, so no total. Card: Single NYJ +3.5 ($10) for the hook, and the NYJ moneyline is one of the six dogs in the Slot 2 Dog-ML 2-team RR. NYJ +3.5 is a SuperContest alternate.

What breaks it: Keenum starts instead of Bagent, which is the case the BettingPros CHI pick rests on, and the Bears pass better than this script assumes. Chicago's 59-point opener shows the ceiling. A Jets turnover in their own end flips a three-point game into a seven-point one. If the number drops back to −3, the hook is gone and so is the lean.

Card evidence: NYJ passing offense vs CHI defense HIGH; Bagent starts; Fezzik, Tucker, Middleton, Action Network, Reynolds NYJ; projection CHI by 3 · full game write-up

🐶 Tennessee Titans +492 — TEN@BAL · tier 2 · our projection TEN 16 – BAL 26

Why it's on the ticket: TEN: Steve Fezzik ("best bet"), Ross Tucker (2 units) Kendra Middleton (the Ravens' long flight home and injuries) and Dave Tuley of VSiN (a best bet). BAL: Brandon Anderson (−11.5 and his contest pick), BettingPros, Sharp or Square (first half only, to avoid a second-half backdoor) and Mike Florio (Ravens 30–17). Splits: BAL has 66% of spread tickets and 71% of the money, but the TEN moneyline is a big-money flag, 4% of tickets and 19% of the money. Evan Abrams' primer has two systems on Tennessee (fading no-pedigree favorites, and fading the public after a poor offensive game), and Baltimore's starting center is out for two to three months. The line is unchanged from the Action Network open at −11.5; the total is down from 43.5 to 43. The lean is TEN +11.5, or BAL first half as Sharp or Square plays it; both fit a script where Baltimore leads early and Tennessee covers late. BettingPros (43.5) and Andrew Erickson (42.5) have the over, but with rain and a projected 42 the total is a pass. Card: the TEN moneyline (+492) is the long leg of the Slot 2 Dog-ML 2-team RR, and TEN +11.5 is a proposed SuperContest pick (both SuperContest tickets). Derrick Henry 2+ TDs is in the 8b 2+ TD 3-leg.

What breaks it: The patched Baltimore line holds, Henry gets 30 carries and the Ravens win by 17. Ward turns it over twice (Sharp or Square calls him regressing). Flowers plays a full game and stretches the field Tennessee is trying to shrink.

Card evidence: Big-money flag (4% tickets / 19% money); Tuley/Fezzik/Tucker TEN +11.5; the long leg of the RR · full game write-up
